messages:
emma_support: Hey team — Acme (acct: acme-prod) just escalated: p95/p99 for /v1/generate spiked starting ~09:10 UTC and they're seeing intermittent 5xx and auth failures. Customer says high latency + 500s on many requests. I have sample request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Can SRE take a look? :eyes:

josh_sre: on it. Do we have any deploys or provisioning events around 09:00-09:15?

deploy-bot: canary-deploy/model-server v2.14 -> v2.15 started 2024-05-14T09:04:22Z

maya_oncall: I see elevated attach latencies for dedicated-pool-acme between 09:08-09:12 in the traces. p99 attach time jumped to ~18s. Provisioner queue length spiked to ~48.

tim_infra: pool logs show many attach failures with: 
```
error: attach failed: no free device
status: 503
detail: pool capacity exhausted
```
Also a few auth errors: 
```
2024-05-14T09:10:33Z WARN auth: token validation failed for token id=redacted, err=KMS:decryption failed (403)
```
Not sure if those are related or coincident.

emma_support: customer reported both 500 responses and some 403 auth errors. They said retries sometimes succeed. They attached a stack trace where response body is a 502 from the attach service.

josh_sre: hypothesis: the canary caused a brief thundering attach pattern + some tokens failing validation causing load to shift to fallback codepath which did extra work. Two contributing factors -> p99 spike. Steps: 1) check dedicated pool true utilization and warmup state, 2) correlate token validation failures to our KMS region, 3) revert canary if needed.

maya_oncall: Provisioner metrics: active_gpus=24, in_use=24, queued_attaches=49, attach_rate=120r/s (normal 40r/s). We hit the hard limit of 24 GPUs for that pool. Autoscaler looked at metrics and queued requests but backoff prevented immediate scaling because provisioning budget exhausted (we were at max for that reservation).

tim_infra: KMS team — I see a short 09:09-09:11 spike in KMS throttle errors in eu-west-1. Those correspond to some token decrypts. If token validation fails, clients sometimes retry and the request ends up on a fallback path that does additional validation and a cold attach. That explains extra attach load.

emma_support: customer wants root cause and mitigation. They've been affected for ~15m and are asking for credit.

josh_sre: immediate mitigation options we can try now: 
- increase dedicated-pool-acme capacity by +2 GPUs (if we can borrow from reserved pool)
- enable temporary burst capacity for that tenant (allow short-lived extra attach slots)
- revert canary to reduce attach storm if canary is implicated
- implement quick rate-limit per-tenant to shed excess parallel attaches (short term)

maya_oncall: I'm going to attempt a manual capacity bump + warmup. Prewarming step: attach fake warmup requests to load KV caches on new GPUs.

tim_infra: I'll open an ops ticket to ask KMS to investigate the throttle and patch any hotspots; also increasing KMS retry/backoff on our side might reduce 403 churn.

deploy-bot: rollback request queued: canary rollback v2.15 -> v2.14 (initiated by josh_sre)

josh_sre: Action log: 09:22 bump pool +2 GPUs to 26 (manual allocation), kicked warmup at 09:23, rollback started 09:24.

emma_support: I told the customer we're doing a manual capacity bump and rolling back the canary, asked for severity and if they want a conference call. They replied: please keep me posted, conference call if impact continues.

acme_ops: Confirming we saw lots of 500s and some 403s; after ~09:30 things improved but there were intermittent failures until ~09:40. We can share traces if helpful.

maya_oncall: Post-mitigation metrics: queued_attaches down from 49 -> 3 by 09:28, attach p99 reduced to ~1.1s by 09:33, generation p99 back to ~700ms by 09:36. Customer reports error rate fell to baseline.

josh_sre: Preliminary RCA: two root causes in combination — (A) KMS region experienced transient throttling causing token validation failures and retries; (B) a canary release changed attach behavior (slightly higher concurrency per request) leading to a short attach storm that saturated dedicated-pool-acme capacity. When token failures caused clients to hit fallback codepaths, attach demand multiplied. The pool was at its hard cap so autoscaler couldn't react fast enough.

tim_infra: Follow-ups: 
- KMS: add circuit-breaker and increase retry/backoff on decrypts for our auth clients (short term).
- Autoscaler: review hard limits and consider a small burst headroom for dedicated pools to absorb attach spikes.
- Runtime: make canary attach concurrency opt-in in early rollout or add a randomized attach backoff to avoid thundering herd.
- Support: offer Acme a credit for the 30m impact window and propose a reserved + burst capacity plan if they expect higher concurrency.

emma_support: I'll draft the customer note + credit proposal.

acme_ops: thanks — can you also add a flag we can set to pin us to a warm pool while we run tests? That would help.

josh_sre: Noted. We'll add a short-term opt-in pinning feature for dedicated customers (manual flag) so you can pin to already-warmed GPUs. We'll track as a product backlog item.

maya_oncall: closing thread for now, monitoring for 2 hours. If anything re-occurs we'll reopen and do a postmortem. :white_check_mark:
